title: Acoustic Lottery: an integrated low-complexity, device-robust acoustic scene classification (ASC) framework
content: Acoustic Lottery is a unified operational framework for low-complexity, device-robust acoustic scene classification that composes the following modules into a single pipeline: (a) data augmentation (mixup; SpecAugment; spectrum correction; pitch shift; speed change; random noise; mix audios) to improve generalization across recording devices; (b) teacher-student learning (TSL) / knowledge distillation where student logits $p_{student}=softmax(\frac{\alpha_{student}}{\tau})$ are trained to match softened teacher outputs at temperature $\tau$ via a Kullback–Leibler distillation loss; (c) iterative Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) pruning search to identify sparse trainable sub-networks from a seed architecture; (d) two-stage score fusion or multi-task learning (MTL) using a 3-class (in-door/out-door/transportation) auxiliary classifier jointly or in fusion with the 10-class main classifier to exploit label abstraction; and (e) post-training dynamic range quantization (DRQ) converting 32-bit floating-point weights to 8-bit integers and dynamically quantizing activations. The framework is explicitly designed to produce ASC models that preserve device-robust predictive performance while meeting strict non-zero-parameter size budgets required for on-device deployment.

title: Iterative Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) pruning procedure adapted for device-robust acoustic scene classification (ASC)
content: An operational LTH pruning algorithm adapted to device-robust ASC is defined as follows. Let $G_0$ denote the chosen seed network architecture and $\Theta_0$ its random initialization. Given augmented training data $D$, the algorithm iterates for $t=1,\ldots,T$ pruning-search iterations: for each iteration perform $E$ epochs of teacher-student training (TSL) to obtain final weights $\Theta_t$ for the current graph $G_t$; if $t<T$, compute a binary mask on $\Theta_t$ (Mask($\Theta_t$)) to obtain a pruned subgraph $G_p$ drawn as a subgraph of $G_0$, then recover the homologous subset of the original initialization $\Theta_p\subset\Theta_0$ (weights from $\Theta_0$ corresponding to the surviving parameters in $G_p$), and set $G_{t+1}(\Theta_p)$ as the next model to train. The algorithm outputs the trained pruned model $G_T(\Theta_T)$. Empirically, on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 Task 1a data the procedure requires only one or two pruning-search iterations ($T=1$ or $2$) to find high-quality low-complexity models.

title: Small-weights masking yields better accuracy–compression trade-off among evaluated Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) mask strategies
content: Among three evaluated Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) mask-selection strategies—(i) large-final, (ii) small-weights, and (iii) global small-weights—the small-weights masking strategy was empirically selected because it produced a superior trade-off between classification accuracy and compression rate on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 Task 1a validation experiments.

title: Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) pruning discovers highly sparse acoustic scene classification (ASC) sub-networks with preserved predictive performance (visualized up to 149× compression)
content: The iterative Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) pruning search procedure—which, starting from a seed network $G_0$ with random initialization $\Theta_0$, repeats for $T$ iterations: train via teacher-student learning on augmented data to obtain weights $\Theta_t$, then if $t<T$ compute a binary mask on $\Theta_t$ to obtain a pruned subgraph $G_p$ from $G_0$, load the homologous subset of initial weights $\Theta_p \subset \Theta_0$ corresponding to surviving parameters, and set the next model $G_{t+1}=G_p(\Theta_p)$; output the trained pruned model $G_T(\Theta_T)$—applied to Inception-based student architectures yields sparse subnetworks that retain or modestly change validation predictive metrics compared to their unpruned seeds while achieving very large parameter reduction; visualization and empirical examples demonstrate discovered models with sparsity corresponding to up to a 149× compression rate in the examined shallow Inception student model.

title: Empirical top-line: ensemble of Large Inception (LIC) and Shallow Inception (SIC) models attains 79.4% validation accuracy and 0.640 log loss
content: An ensemble built from pruned and distilled Large Inception (LIC) and Shallow Inception (SIC) models under the Acoustic Lottery pipeline achieved a validation accuracy of $79.4\%$ and a log loss of $0.640$ on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 Task 1a development set, demonstrating that the integrated compression-and-training workflow can reach high predictive performance comparable to much larger prior systems while using compressed components.

title: Compressed ensemble meeting the 128 KB non-zero-parameter constraint: ensemble of Large Inception (LIC) models achieves 78.7% accuracy with 117 KB size
content: An ensemble composed of pruned and distilled Large Inception (LIC) models produced a system with 117 KB non-zero parameters, validation accuracy $78.7\%$, and log loss $0.644$ on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 Task 1a development set, thereby demonstrating that the Acoustic Lottery approach can produce multi-device-robust acoustic scene classification (ASC) systems meeting the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) Task 1a size constraint.

title: Teacher-Student Learning increases student validation accuracy and reduces log loss for Shallow Inception (SIC)
content: Applying teacher-student learning (TSL) to the Shallow Inception (SIC) student model improved validation accuracy from $67.8\%$ to $68.9\%$ and reduced log loss from $0.954$ to $0.919$ on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 development set, demonstrating that distillation of a large two-stage teacher into a small student increases the student model's predictive performance under acoustic scene classification (ASC) multi-device conditions.

title: Dynamic range post-training quantization (DRQ) reduces numeric footprint ~4× and, combined with Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) pruning, enables sub-128 KB Large Inception (LIC) models (example: 103 KB, 78.2% accuracy)
content: Post-training dynamic range quantization (DRQ) that statically quantizes weights to 8-bit integers and dynamically quantizes activations reduces model file size by roughly a factor of four versus 32-bit storage; when applied after Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) pruning and teacher-student learning (TSL), this quantization produced a Large Inception (LIC)-based system with 103 KB non-zero-parameter size, validation accuracy $78.2\%$, and log loss $0.723$ on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 Task 1a development set, demonstrating that DRQ can be used in concert with sparse-subnetwork discovery to reach stringent size budgets.

title: Practical pruning depth: one or two Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) search iterations sufficient for acoustic scene classification (ASC)
content: Empirically on the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) 2021 Task 1a data, the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH) pruning search—which repeatedly trains the model via teacher-student learning, prunes by masking weights, and resets surviving weights to their initial random values—required only $T=1$ or $T=2$ pruning-search iterations to find high-quality low-complexity acoustic models that do not suffer significant validation accuracy degradation compared to their high-complexity teachers.
